title: Resolving Power of Optical Instruments
short_intro: The resolving power of an optical instrument is its ability to distinguish between two closely spaced point objects as separate entities. It is fundamentally limited by the diffraction of light waves at the aperture of the instrument.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Rayleigh's criterion for resolution, resolving power of microscopes and telescopes, dependence on wavelength and aperture size.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Quantitative derivation of resolving power for rectangular and circular apertures, diffraction grating resolution, Rayleigh limit for spectral lines.

prerequisites: Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit and circular aperture

concept_notes.heading: Rayleigh Criterion for Resolution
bullets: Two point sources are resolved if the principal maximum of the diffraction pattern of one falls exactly over the first minimum of the diffraction pattern of the other.
When the central maximum of one pattern coincides with the central maximum of the other such that their separation is less than the Rayleigh limit, the sources are unresolved.
At the limit of resolution, the dip between the two central maxima in the combined intensity distribution is approximately 20% lower than the maximum intensity.

concept_notes.heading: Resolving Power of a Microscope
bullets: Resolving power of a microscope is defined as the reciprocal of the minimum linear distance between two point objects that can be separately distinguished.
It is directly proportional to the numerical aperture of the objective lens and inversely proportional to the wavelength of light used for illumination.
Oil immersion objectives are used to increase the refractive index of the medium between the object and the objective, thereby enhancing resolving power.

concept_notes.heading: Resolving Power of a Telescope
bullets: Resolving power of a telescope is defined as the reciprocal of the smallest angular separation (dθ) between two distant point objects whose images can be resolved.
It is directly proportional to the diameter of the objective lens or mirror and inversely proportional to the wavelength of light.
Larger aperture telescopes are required to resolve closely spaced binary stars or fine details on planetary surfaces.

concept_notes.heading: Resolving Power of a Diffraction Grating
bullets: The resolving power of a diffraction grating measures its ability to form separate diffraction maxima for two nearby wavelengths (λ and λ + dλ).
It depends directly on the total number of rulings on the grating and the order of the diffraction spectrum.
It is expressed mathematically as R = (lambda / dlambda) = Nn, where N is total lines and n is spectral order.

derivations.title: Resolving Power of a Telescope
derivations.conditions: Fraunhofer diffraction by a circular aperture of diameter D
steps: The first minimum of the diffraction pattern produced by a circular aperture of diameter D occurs at an angular position given by sin(θ) = 1.22 (λ / D).
Therefore, the minimum angular separation for two point objects to be resolved according to Rayleigh's criterion is dθ = 1.22 (λ / D).

derivations.title: Resolving Power of a Microscope
derivations.conditions: Light of wavelength λ entering an objective of semi-vertical angle u in a medium of refractive index μ
steps: The limit of resolution (minimum distance d) for a circular aperture is given by Abbe's theory combined with Rayleigh's criterion as d = (λ / (2 μ sin(u))).
The term μ sin(u) is known as the Numerical Aperture (NA) of the microscope.
Resolving Power (RP) is the reciprocal of the limit of resolution d.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Intensity Distribution for Two Resolved Point Sources
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Two overlapping single-slit diffraction intensity curves where the central maximum of one coincides with the first minimum of the other, showing a clear dip of about 20% in the center.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Represents the Rayleigh criterion limit where two point sources are just resolved by an optical instrument.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Directly tested in conceptual questions regarding the intensity profile at the limit of resolution.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Intensity Distribution for Unresolved Sources
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Two diffraction curves whose angular separation is less than λ/D, resulting in a single broad peak with an insufficient central dip.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Indicates that the optical instrument cannot distinguish the two sources as separate objects.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Contrasted with the resolved state in multiple-choice questions.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Michelson's Stellar Interferometer Experiment
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Schematic setup showing two movable mirrors receiving light from a distant star to create interference fringes.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Used to determine the angular diameter of distant stars by finding the fringe disappearance separation.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Advanced PGT application of resolving power concepts to stellar astronomy.

solved_numericals.question: A telescope has an objective lens of diameter 1.0 m. Calculate its resolving power for light of wavelength 550 nm.
solution_steps: Identify given values: D = 1.0 m, \lambda = 550 \text{ nm} = 5.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}.
Use the formula for resolving power of a telescope: RP = D / (1.22 \lambda).

solved_numericals.question: Light of wavelength 6000 Å is incident on a microscope objective with a numerical aperture of 0.12. Find the limit of resolution.
solution_steps: Use the formula for limit of resolution of a microscope: d = \lambda / (2 \text{ NA}).

solved_numericals.question: A diffraction grating has 500 lines per cm and is 5 cm wide. Find its resolving power in the second order for a wavelength of 5000 Å.
solution_steps: Find the total number of lines N = (lines per cm) \times (width in cm) = 500 \text{ cm}^{-1} \times 5 \text{ cm} = 2500.
Identify order n = 2 and wavelength \lambda = 5000 \text{ Å}.
Use the formula for resolving power of a grating: R = N n.

assumptions_and_limitations: Rayleigh's criterion assumes incoherent point sources of equal intensity.
The analysis assumes Fraunhofer diffraction conditions (source and screen at infinity or via lenses).
Aberrations in optical lenses are neglected when calculating theoretical resolving power limits.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Magnification and resolving power mean the same thing for an optical instrument.
common_misconceptions.correct: Magnification enlarges the image size, whereas resolving power allows two close details to be distinguished separately.
common_misconceptions.why: An image can be made arbitrarily large (high magnification) without adding any new structural details if the resolving power is insufficient.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Decreasing the wavelength of light decreases the resolving power of a microscope.
common_misconceptions.correct: Shorter wavelengths increase the resolving power.
common_misconceptions.why: Resolving power is inversely proportional to wavelength (λ); hence, ultraviolet or electron beams provide higher resolution than visible light.

quick_revision: Telescope resolving power increases with larger objective diameter D.
Microscope resolving power increases with higher numerical aperture (NA) and shorter wavelength (λ).
Grating resolving power depends solely on total lines N and spectral order n.
